title: The legend of Shunahshepa
introduction: The Legend of Shunashepa is commenced and Sage Shataananda continues this as a part of Vishvamitra's legend. When Rama's grandparent Ambariisha undertook a ritual, Indra impounds that ritual's horse. Then Ambariisha had to fetch a human-animal in lieu of that lost horse. When none is available one named Shunashepa, son of Sage Riciika, and a nephew of Vishvamitra, offers himself with a barter of riches to his parents.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 61st chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रो महातेजाः प्रस्थितान् वीक्ष्य तानृषीन् |
अब्रवीन्नरशार्दूल सर्वांस्तान् वनवासिनः
verses.iast:
viśvāmitro mahātejāḥ prasthitān vīkśya tān ṛṣīn |
abravīt naraśārdūla sarvān tān vana vāsinaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, manly-tiger Rama, on giving farewell to those sages who came at his invitation and who have started to go back after the ritual of Trishanku is over, then that great-resplendent Vishvamitra spoke to all of the sages who are forest dwellers that remained with him." Thus Shatananda continued to narrate the legend of Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: those who started to go back

verses.devanagari:
महान् विघ्नः प्रवृत्तोऽयं दक्षिणामास्थितो दिशम् |
दिशमन्यां प्रपत्स्यामस्तत्र तप्स्यामहे तपः
verses.iast:
mahāvighnaḥ pravṛtto ayam dakṣiṇām āsthito diśam |
diśam anyām prapatsyāmaḥ tatra tapsyāmahe tapaḥ
verses.translation: " 'While depending on this southern quarter this gross hindrance has cropped up for my ascesis in the shape of Trishanku's ascent to heaven, hence we will go to another direction, and there we continue ascesis.

glosses.meaning: this [Trishanku's episode,] a gross, hindrance, cropped up

verses.devanagari:
पश्चिमायां विशालायां पुष्करेषु महात्मनः |
सुखं तपश्चरिष्यामः परं तद्धि तपोवनम्
verses.iast:
paścimāyām viśālāyām puṣkareṣu mahātmanaḥ |
sukham tapaḥ cariṣyāmaḥ param tat hi tapo vanam
verses.translation: " 'Oh, great-souled sages, we can conveniently undertake our ascesis in the vast of westerly direction where holy lakesides are there. That would be an august ascetical forest, isn't it.' Thus Vishvamitra said to fellow sages in his camp.

glosses.meaning: that is, august, ascetical, forest, isn't it.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः पुष्करेषु महामुनिः |
तप उग्रं दुराधर्षं तेपे मूलफलाशनः
verses.iast:
evam uktvā mahātejāḥ puṣkareṣu mahāmuniḥ |
tapa ugram durādharṣam tepe mūla phala aśanaḥ
verses.translation: "On saying thus that most brilliant and great saint Vishvamitra performed an unhindered and rigorous ascesis subsisting only on fruits and tubers after reaching the lakeside of holy lakes.

glosses.meaning: in holy lakeside - after reaching them

verses.devanagari:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु अयोध्याधिपतिर्महान् |
अंबरीष इति ख्यातो यष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
verses.iast:
etasmin eva kāle tu ayodhyā adhipatiḥ mahān |
ambarīṣa iti khyāto yaṣṭum samupacakrame
verses.translation: "In the meanwhile the great king of Ayodhya, renowned as Ambariisha, embarked on to perform a Vedic-ritual.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य वै यजमानस्य पशुमिन्द्रो जहार ह |
प्रणष्टे तु पशौ विप्रो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tasya vai yajamānasya paśum indro jahāra ha |
praṇaṣṭe tu paśau vipro rājānam idam abravīt
verses.translation: "But Indra impounded the animal of the principal of that ritual, namely king Ambariisha, and when that animal is really vanished, the officiant Brahman of the ritual spoke this to that king.

glosses.meaning: of the principal [of ritual,] his, ritual-animal
animal is, verily lost [really vanished,] while becoming
the officiant of ritual, to king, this, spoke.

verses.devanagari:
पशुरभ्याहृतो राजन् प्रणष्टस्तव दुर्नयात् |
अरक्षितारं राजानं घ्नन्ति दोषा नरेश्वर
verses.iast:
paśuḥ abhyāhṛtaḥ rājan praṇaṣṭaḥ tava dur.hnayāt |
arakṣitāram rājānam ghnanti doṣā nareśvara
verses.translation: " 'Oh, king, the animal you have fetched for the ritual has gone astray owing to your incautiousness. Oh, king, unguarded items of the ritual will themselves become destructive blemishes for that king who is performing the ritual.

glosses.meaning: for king, as blemishes, will destruct.

verses.devanagari:
प्रायश्चित्तं महद्ध्येतन्नरं वा पुरुषर्षभ |
आनयस्व पशुं शीघ्रं यावत् कर्म प्रवर्तते
verses.iast:
prāyaḥ cittam mahat hi etat naram vā puruṣarṣabha |
ānayasva paśum śīghram yāvat karma pravar.htate
verses.translation: " 'Oh, the best man among men, you have to make great amends for the loss of animal as that animal alone which was intended but now missing shall be used in ritual. Or, a man may be fetched as ritual-animal, and only after that the deeds of the ritual can be continued.' Thus, the priests of the ritual said to king Ambariisha.

glosses.meaning: a great, making amends - is to be done
ritual-deeds, until [only after that,] will continue.

verses.devanagari:
उपाध्यायवचः श्रुत्वा स राजा पुरुषर्षभ |
अन्वियेष महाबुद्धिः पशुं गोभिः सहस्रशः
verses.iast:
upādhyāya vacaḥ śrutvā sa rājā puruṣarṣabha |
anviyeṣa mahābuddhiḥ paśum gobhiḥ sahasraśaḥ
verses.translation: "On hearing the words of his teacher, oh, the best one among men, Rama, he that highly rule-obedient king tried for a human-ritual-animal for a barter of thousands of cows.

glosses.meaning: highly intelligent [obedient king to rules,] king

verses.devanagari:
देशान् जनपदांस्तांस्तान्नगराणि वनानि च |
आश्रमाणि च पुण्यानि मार्गमाणो महीपतिः
स पुत्रसहितं तात सभार्यं रघुनंदन |
भृगुतुंगे समासीनमृचीकं संददर्श ह
verses.iast:
deśān janapadān tān tān nagarāṇi vanāni ca |
āśramāṇi ca puṇyāni mārgamāṇo mahīpatiḥ
sa putra sahitam tāta sa bhāryam raghunandana |
bhṛgutuṅge samāsīnam ṛcīkam sandadarśa ha
verses.translation: "While that king is searching those and those provinces, villages, forests, townships, and even the pious hermitages, oh, dear Rama, the legatee of Raghu's dynasty, that king has indeed seen Sage Riciika, who is well settled on Mt. Bhrigutunga along with his sons and wife.

glosses.meaning: he that land, lord - that king Ambariisha
at Sage Raiciika, well, he has seen, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
तमुवाच महातेजाः प्रणम्याभिप्रसाद्य च |
महर्षिं तपसा दीप्तं राजर्षिरमितप्रभः
पृष्ट्वा सर्वत्र कुशलमृचीकं तमिदं वचः |
verses.iast:
tam uvāca mahātejāḥ praṇaṃya abhiprasādya ca |
maharṣim tapasā dīptam rājarṣiḥ amita prabhaḥ
pṛṣṭvā sarvatra kuśalam ṛcīkam tam idam vacaḥ |
verses.translation: "On reverencing and on obtaining the grace of ascetically brilliant great Sage Riciika, and even on asking him about his wellbeing in every aspect, that kingly sage Ambariisha, who is with great resplendence and whose brilliance is illimitable, said this word to that sage.

glosses.meaning: in every aspect, wellbeing, on asking
this, word, said - King Ambariisha said.

verses.devanagari:
गवां शतसहस्रेण विक्रीणीषे सुतं यदि
पशोरर्थे महाभाग कृतकृत्योऽस्मि भार्गव |
verses.iast:
gavām śata sahasreṇa vikrīṇīṣe sutam yadi
paśoḥ arthe mahābhāga kṛta kṛtyo asmi bhārgava |
verses.translation: " 'Oh, godlike sage, if you bargain your son with a hundred thousand cows for the purpose of a ritual-animal, oh, the successor Sage Bhrigu, I deem my ends are achieved.

glosses.meaning: done, deed [achieved ends,] I will be.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वे परिगता देशा यज्ञियं न लभे पशुम्
दातुमर्हसि मूल्येन सुतमेकमितो मम |
verses.iast:
sarve parigatā deśā yajñiyam na labhe paśum
dātum ar.hhasi mūlyena sutam ekam ito mama |
verses.translation: " 'All the provinces are went over but unobtainable is that animal of the ritual, hence it will be apt of you to give me one son from among your sons, for a value.' Thus, king Ambariisha bargained with the sage.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तो महातेजा ऋचीकस्त्वब्रवीद्वचः
नाहं ज्येष्ठं नरश्रेष्ठ विक्रीणीयां कथंचन |
verses.iast:
evam ukto mahātejā ṛcīkaḥ tu abravīt vacaḥ
na aham jyeṣṭham nara śreṣṭha vikrīṇīyām kathañcana |
verses.translation: "When that great-resplendent Sage Riciika is addressed thus, he said this word, 'oh, best of men, I cannot possibly sell my eldest son, in anyway.'

glosses.meaning: oh, man, the best - king Ambariisha

verses.devanagari:
ऋचीकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा तेषां माता महात्मनाम्
उवाच नरशार्दूलमंबरीषमिदं वचः |
verses.iast:
ṛcīkasya vacaḥ śrutvā teṣām mātā mahātmanām
uvāca nara śārdūlam ambarīṣam idam vacaḥ |
verses.translation: "On hearing the words of Sage Riciika the mother of those great-souled sons spoke this word to the tigerly-man Ambariisha.

verses.devanagari:
अविक्रेयं सुतं ज्येष्ठं भगवानाह भार्गवः
ममापि दयितं विद्धि कनिष्ठं शुनकं प्रभो |
तस्मात् कनीयसं पुत्रं न दास्ये तव पार्थिव
verses.iast:
avikreyam sutam jyeṣṭham bhagavān āha bhārgavaḥ
mama api dayitam viddhi kaniṣṭham śunakam prabho |
tasmāt kanīyasam putram na dāsye tava pārthiva
verses.translation: "The most reverential sage and the one from Bhaargava dynasty, my husband, said that the eldest son is un-sellable. Thereof oh, lord, you must know that my youngest son, namely Shunaka, is a cherished one for me. Therefore oh, king, I will not give my youngest son to you, either.

glosses.meaning: to you not, I will give.

verses.devanagari:
प्रायेण हि नरश्रेष्ठ ज्येष्ठाः पितृषु वल्लभाः |
मातॄणां च कनीयांसस्तस्माद्रक्षे कनीयसम्
verses.iast:
prāyeṇa hi naraśreṣṭha jyeṣṭhāḥ pitṛṣu vallabhāḥ |
mātṝṇām ca kanīyāṃsaḥ tasmāt rakṣe kanīyasam
verses.translation: "Generally eldest sons are fathers' favourites, oh, best king among men, and mothers' favourites are the youngest, isn't it! Therefor, I have to tend my youngest son.' Thus, wife Sage Ruciika said to Ambariisha.
notes: The wife of the Sage Ruciika is Satyavathi, the sister of Vishvamitra whose legend was narrated by Vishvamitra in Bala Ch. 34. This longing for youngest sons by a mother is reflected in Maha Bharata, where Kunti pleads for leaving Sahadeva, the youngest Pandava, from going to forest exile, along with her in the city. In sabhā parva she says: sabhā parvāṇi sahadevam prati kuntī vākyam - sahadeva nivartasva nanu tvam asi me priyaḥ | śarīrāt api mādreya māmatyakṣīḥ kuputravat | - āśrama vāse dharma putram prati kuntī vākyam - sahadeva mārāja mā pramādam kṛthā | - dk Kunti, the mother of Pandava-s says: 'oh, Sahadeva, you refrain from going on exile as you are a dear son of mine, though Maadri gave you a bodily birth, you are my favourite...' Also, in the period of forest exile she says to Yudhishtar: 'oh, king, let no danger occur to Sahadeva... as he is my cherished son...'

glosses.meaning: oh, best one among men - oh, king
eldest [sons,] for father, favourites, isn't it
therefor, I [have to] tend, youngest one.

verses.devanagari:
उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन् मुनिपत्न्यां तथैव च |
शुनःशेपः स्वयं राम मध्यमो वाक्यमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
ukta vākye munau tasmin muni patnyām tathaiva ca |
śunaḥśepaḥ svayam rāma madhyamo vākyam abravīt
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, when that sage's sentence is so, and his wife's sentence is also in that way only, their intermediate son, namely Shunashepa, personally spoke this sentence.

glosses.meaning: by sage, wife's, in that way, only

verses.devanagari:
पिता ज्येष्ठमविक्रेयं माता चाह कनीयसम् |
विक्रेतं मध्यमं मन्ये राजपुत्र नयस्व माम्
verses.iast:
pitā jyeṣṭham avikreyam mātā ca āha kanīyasam |
vikretam madhyamam manye rājaputra nayasva mām
verses.translation: " 'Father said that the eldest son is un-sellable, mother also said the same about youngest one. Then I deem that the intermediary son is sellable. Hence, oh, prince, you may lead me forth.

glosses.meaning: father eldest one, as un-sellable one, he is telling
mother, also [said the same, about] youngest son

verses.devanagari:
अथ राजा महाबाहो वाक्यान्ते ब्रह्मवादिनः |
हिरण्यस्य सुवर्णस्य कोटिभी रत्नराशिभिः
गवां शतसहस्रेण शुनःशेपं नरेश्वरः |
गृहीत्वा परमप्रीतो जगाम रघुनंदन
verses.iast:
atha rājā mahābāho vākya ante brahma vādinaḥ |
hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya koṭibhī ratna rāśibhiḥ
gavām śata sahasreṇa śunaḥśepam nareśvaraḥ |
gṛhītvā parama prīto jagāma raghunandana
verses.translation: "Oh, dextrous Rama, when that advocate of Veda-s, namely Shunashepa finished his speech, then the king gave gold, silver, and gemstones, each in ten million heaps, and even a hundred thousand cows, and oh, Rama, the legatee of Ragu, that king Ambariisha went away highly gladdened to take Shunashepa with him.

glosses.meaning: sentence, end of [when he finished his speech]

verses.devanagari:
अंबरीषस्तु राजर्षी रथमारोप्य सत्वरः |
शुनःशेपं महातेजा जगामाशु महायशाः
verses.iast:
ambarīṣaḥ tu rājar.hṣī ratham āropya satvaraḥ |
śunaḥśepam mahātejā jagāma āśu mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: "That great resplendent and highly renowned king Ambariisha on his part proceeded hastily after ascending Shunashepa onto the chariot that hastily." Thus Sage Shataananda continued his narration.

glosses.meaning: highly renowned - king raajarSii ambariiSaH tu = kingly sage, Ambariisha, on his part
